senses.gloss: to come, come in. Perf. עָל, עָאל; part. עָל, עָאֵיל, עָאֵל, עָיֵיל.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 7:23">Targ. O. Ex. VII, 23</cite> <he>על</he>; Targ. Y. <cite ref="P00003"><he>עאל</he></cite> (ed. Amst. <cite ref="A02592"><he>אָעַל</he></cite>). Targ. Y. ib. XXXIII, 9 <cite ref="P00003"><he>עאיל</he></cite> (ed. Amst. <cite ref="P00241"><he>אָעֵיל</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 23:10">Targ. O. Gen. XXIII, 10</cite> <he>עָאלֵי</he> (ed. Berl. a. oth. <cite ref="P00791"><he>עָלֵי</he></cite>; Y. <cite ref="P00791"><he>עֲלֵי</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 17:10">Targ. Prov. XVII, 10</cite> <he>עָאלָא</he> ed. Lag. (oth. ed. <cite ref="P00565"><he>עָלָא</he></cite>); a. fr.—Y. Kidd. II, 63ᵃ top <he>דחק סומכוס ועאל</he> S. pressed on and went in.
<cite ref="Yoma 51b:8">Yoma 51ᵇ</cite> <he>נֵיעוּל וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>נעביד</he>) let him make his entrance in the way prescribed by R. J.
<cite ref="Yoma 52a:2">Ib. 52ᵃ</cite> <he>ניעול בין מנורה וכ׳</he> let him make his entrance between the candlestick and the wall.
<cite ref="Pesachim 112a">Pes. 112ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 21a:12">B. Bath. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>שבשתא כיון דעל על</he> a mistake once entered (into the mind) remains therein.
<cite ref="Shabbat 98b:4">Sabb. 98ᵇ</cite> <he>האי עָיֵיל והאי נפיק</he> one will go in (recede), the other go out (protrude, i.e. form an uneven surface.); a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 6:19">Targ. Y. Gen. VI, 19</cite> <he>תֵעוֹל</he> ed. Vien. (v. <cite ref="P00816"><he>עֲלַל</he></cite>).—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 67:7">Gen. R. s. 67</cite> (ref. to <he>ועל חרבך</he> <cite ref="Genesis 27:40">Gen. XXVII, 40</cite>) <he>עול חרבך וכ׳</he> bring thy sword home (into its sheath), and thou shalt live; (Yalk. ib. 115 <he>תטול</he>, read: <he>תֵּעוּל</he>).

senses.gloss: to come in habitually. Inf. מְעַיֵּיל, v. מֵעֲלָא.

units: <cite ref="Eruvin 44b:6">Erub. 44ᵇ</cite> <he>בעי עַיְּילִינְהוּ</he> wanted to bring them in.

<cite ref="Shabbat 96b:4">Sabb. 96ᵇ</cite> <he>מה לי אפוקי ומה לי עַיּיוּלֵי</he> what is the difference between carrying out and bringing in? <cite ref="Eruvin 38b:8">Erub. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>ע׳ רב חסדא וכ׳</he> R. Ḥ. brought (the subject) in, in order to show a contradiction &c.
<cite ref="Ketubot 101a:13">Ib. 101ᵃ</cite> <he>עַיְּילָא ליה גלימא</he> if she brought him a cloak (as dowry).
<cite ref="Yoma 47a:4">Yoma 47ᵃ</cite> <he>נְעַיֵּיל והדר נעייל</he> shall he bring in (one portion) and again bring in (another portion)?; a. fr.

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 13a:1">R. Hash. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>ודילמא לא ע׳ כלל</he> perhaps it means when it (the growing vegetation) had not yet begun to ripen at all? <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 13a">Ib.</cite> <he>דע׳ ביד נכרי</he> the barley of which the ‘Omer was brought had ripened while in the possession of a gentile (a Canaanite).
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 13a">Ib.</cite> <he>דע׳ ריבעא</he> if it has developped one fourth of the full size; a. e.

senses.gloss: to insert one’s self; to get in.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 51b:9">Yoma 51ᵇ</cite> <he>ולא מִתְעַיֵּיל ליה</he> he could not get himself in (between the table and the wall).
